questions.q: Which Qdrant client method does this lesson use for retrieval, and why?
options: query_points(), because the older search() method is deprecated and being removed
search(), because it is the only method that has ever existed
fetch_nearest(), a method unique to this lesson's example
No client method is needed — Qdrant retrieves automatically
questions.explain: The lesson explicitly calls out that Qdrant's current client uses query_points(), since the older search() method is deprecated and scheduled for removal.

questions.q: What must be true about the embedding model used to embed a question at retrieval time?
options: It must be a different, more powerful model than the one used at ingestion
It must be the same embedding model used when the chunks were embedded in Lesson 4
It doesn't matter which embedding model is used, as long as one is used
No embedding is needed at retrieval time, only at ingestion
questions.explain: The lesson is explicit that the question must be embedded with the same model used at ingestion time, so the question's vector lands in the same embedding space as the stored chunks.

questions.q: What does the system prompt's instruction to "say so if the answer isn't in the context" protect against?
options: Slow API response times
Qdrant running out of storage space
The need for chunk metadata entirely
The model filling a gap with a plausible-sounding guess instead of admitting it doesn't know
questions.explain: The lesson frames this instruction as giving the model explicit permission to say "I don't know" rather than hallucinating an answer when the retrieved context doesn't actually contain it.

questions.q: According to this lesson, how do you read your API key when constructing the Anthropic client with Anthropic()?
options: It must be typed directly into the source file as a string literal
It is retrieved from the Qdrant client's configuration
It is read automatically from the ANTHROPIC_API_KEY environment variable
No API key is required to call the Messages API
questions.explain: The lesson states that Anthropic() with no arguments reads the API key from the ANTHROPIC_API_KEY environment variable, and warns against hardcoding a key directly into source.

questions.q: If a generated answer is factually wrong, how does its citation help diagnose the cause?
options: Citations never help diagnose wrong answers
A citation tells you whether the wrong chunks were retrieved, or the right chunks were retrieved but generation still got it wrong
A citation only tells you the current date
A citation automatically fixes the wrong answer
questions.explain: The lesson explains that a citation is a debugging tool: it lets you tell apart a retrieval failure (wrong chunks) from a generation failure (right chunks, wrong answer).
